title: Deployment Strategist
jobDescription:
The Deployment Strategist is embedded inside one of our strategic enterprise customers, paired with a forward deployed engineer and reporting into an Engagement Manager. Your job is to understand the customer's operations better than most of their own employees, frame the highest-leverage problems to solve, and make sure we deliver. You translate a messy, human, operational reality into a clear problem statement, then work with your engineering partner to ship the solution that solves it. The best people in this seat go deep on two fronts at once: the business problem and the technology. You reason from first principles about how an operation actually runs, and you get into the technical detail of how an agent should be built to run it. We care far more about how you think than where you've worked. If you're high agency and go deep, if you'd rather frame and solve a hard operational problem than manage around it, this is your seat. People thrive here from many backgrounds: an ex-founder who wants startup agency with platform leverage; someone who ran a supply-chain or operations function and now wants to build the product rather than buy it; a strategy consultant who loved the operations floor more than the deck. The common thread is depth and ownership, not a logo on your CV. What you'll own Framing the problem. Diagnose the customer's operational reality. Map current state, identify the highest-leverage opportunities, and build a sequenced transformation roadmap with measurable milestones. Pilots and proofs-of-concept. Before the contract is signed, you're in the customer's office running the discovery work that scopes the delivery. The people who will deliver are the people who scope. The customer relationship, from the floor to the boardroom. From operations supervisors up to business-unit heads and CXOs. You become a genuine thought partner to the customer's leaders on how their operation should run, not just the Shipsy face inside the account. Solution design with your engineering partner. They build; you frame. You translate customer intent into clear solution requirements and AI workflow designs. You debate architecture. You sit in the same room. Adoption. Training, workshops, executive briefings, operational rollout. The solution working isn't enough; the customer using it is the metric. Product feedback. Every insight you generate feeds our platform. Patterns you spot today become what the product does tomorrow — for every customer. Industry depth. Build expertise in your assigned vertical (logistics, transport, FMCG, retail). Become the person inside Shipsy whom colleagues ask when they have a question about that industry. Who we're looking for High agency. You decide what matters and drive it without waiting to be told. You have a track record of framing an ambiguous problem and owning the outcome end to end. Depth of thinking. First-principles thinker. You go deeper than the brief, structure what others find chaotic, and aren't satisfied until you understand the real mechanism. Technical depth and curiosity. You go into the hard technical problems, not around them. You can read an API spec, reason about a data pipeline, and have a substantive debate about how an agent should be built. You don't need to code full-stack, but you're genuinely technical and want to be. Thought leadership with the customer's leaders. You earn the right to shape how a customer's CXOs and business heads think about their own operation. They should leave a conversation with you having learned something. That's the bar, not just executive presence. Deep in the business problem. You understand the customer's operation better than most of their own employees. Supply chain, logistics, transport, or retail-operations experience is a real advantage. If you don't have it, show us you ramp fast on a new operational domain. You use AI tools in your work. Claude, GPT, agent frameworks, APIs. We'll ask you to show us what you've built. Background is open. We hire deep, high-agency people from many paths: ex-founders, operators and BU owners inside logistics or supply-chain businesses, strategy consultants (MBB or Big-4 strategy arms), or strong operators from high-growth tech. The path matters less than the depth and the ownership. Tier-1 education. IIT / NIT / BITS / equivalent, or top international institution. Where the role sits You work in a small team — typically one deployment strategist, one or two forward deployed engineers, and a support and training lead — led by an Engagement Manager who owns the overall customer outcome. You report into the Engagement Manager on your account, with a dotted line to the regional Senior Director, Growth Strategy for career development. Travel is significant — expect 40–60% of your time on-site with your customer. The rest, you're in our regional office with the other strategists in your region, comparing patterns and stress-testing each other's roadmaps. Progression is direct: strong strategists move into Engagement Manager roles within 18–30 months. This is the training ground for senior customer-facing leadership at Shipsy. About Shipsy Shipsy is the logistics platform behind some of the largest enterprise supply chains in the world. Carriers, post and parcel operators, retailers, and FMCG companies use us to plan dispatch, run operations, settle invoices, and handle exceptions at global scale. Where we are going. Most enterprise logistics still runs on spreadsheets, legacy ERPs, and tribal knowledge. We are replacing that with software that uses AI where it actually helps. Logistics is a multi-trillion-dollar industry that has been under-served by software for decades. We are changing that. The scale today:
- 275+ enterprise customers across 30+ countries
- 5 billion+ shipments processed annually
- 240+ carrier integrations
- 7 global offices — Gurugram · Bengaluru · Dubai · Riyadh · Sydney · Amsterdam · Singapore
- 300+ team members Who we run: Aramex (65 countries, 18,000+ drivers, $27M annual savings delivered) · Heineken (2M+ trips across 70+ countries) · LATAM Cargo (Latin America's largest airline group, $12B+ annual revenue) · Qatar Post (powers mail to 200+ countries) · Post Luxembourg (50%+ market share, $5M+/year savings) · Teleport (80% of Southeast Asia's air-logistics network) · plus DPD, Smiths News, Apollo Pharmacy, argenx, Flipkart Minutes, Swiggy Instamart, and hundreds more. Backed by $35M+ in venture capital from Peak XV Partners , A91 Partners , Info Edge , and others. Featured in the Gartner Magic Quadrant . SOC 2 Type II , ISO 27001 , and GDPR compliant. 99.7% uptime SLA. Trajectory. 50x revenue growth since
2020. Building toward $100M ARR and a public listing . We are still a startup. Our real scale-up began in 2020 — and we have grown 50x since. Early enough that every senior hire shapes the next decade of the business. You are not joining a steady-state organisation with everything figured out. You will build the playbook, lead the team, and own the outcome — with the speed and agency of a startup and the scale of customers most startups never touch. The Deployment Strategist is one of the most critical new roles we are building. If you have spent your career learning how large, complex operating organisations work — and now want to use that knowledge to ship AI that actually runs them — this is the role.

title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobDescription:
The Forward Deployed Engineer is one of the highest-leverage technical roles at Shipsy. The thesis is simple: the engineers closest to the customer's real problems, with the most context, build the fastest and most valuable things first. What you build for one customer becomes the blueprint for what our platform productises for everyone. You're embedded inside one of our strategic enterprise customers, paired with a deployment strategist, reporting to an Engagement Manager. You configure Shipsy to the customer's reality, build the integrations that make it usable, and ship the agent workflows that make it transformative. This is not an engineering role that sits in a squad shipping tickets. It's an engineer who lives in the customer's operations, understands their world better than most of their own employees, and makes Shipsy work for them personally. What you'll own Configuration. Translate Shipsy's platform into a working implementation for your customer — orchestration flows, business rules, pricing logic, operational workflows. Integrations. SAP, Oracle, TMS, WMS, custom legacy systems — whatever plumbing it takes to make Shipsy the system of action inside the customer's stack. AI agents. Design and deploy dispatch copilots, invoice reconciliation agents, and operational decision layers on Shipsy's agent platform. Ship what the customer needs, fast. Go-live. Own the technical path from pilot to production. When the integration breaks at 2am, you're the one accountable — not a platform team two time zones away. Pairing with your strategist. The deployment strategist frames the problem; you build the solution. Debate, push back, sharpen each other. Neither works in isolation. Product feedback. Every configuration you ship is a product signal. What you build this quarter is what our platform team productises next quarter. Scaling yourself. Use AI tooling aggressively. You should be the person on the team who has automated more of their own work than anyone else. Who we're looking for We hire two complementary profiles. Both are valid; the mix depends on the account. Profile A — Engineering-deep. Strong software engineer from a high-growth technology company. IIT / NIT / BITS or equivalent. 3+ years of production engineering. Comfortable with ambiguity, comfortable owning a customer relationship, comfortable working without a PM spec. Profile B — Transformation-deep. Ex-MBB, GCC banking, or equivalent experience managing large-scale enterprise change programmes — with strong technical curiosity and hands-on AI fluency. Not the engineer who shipped the backend, but the person who figured out why the backend needed to be rewritten. Across both profiles, we're looking for: Entrepreneurial instinct. You've founded something, owned a business unit, or driven a significant initiative end-to-end. You take accountability without being asked. You use AI tools in your work. Claude, GPT, agent frameworks. We'll ask what you've actually built, not what you've read about. Technical credibility. You can work directly with APIs, data pipelines, and agent configuration. You can read unfamiliar code, stand up infrastructure, and debug production issues. Complex stakeholder management. Equally effective in an executive conversation and a ground-level operations environment. Structured problem-solving. First-principles thinker who decomposes ambiguous problems into clear, sequenced, actionable plans. Tier-1 education. IIT / NIT / BITS / equivalent, or top international institution. Where the role sits You work in a small team led by an Engagement Manager, alongside a deployment strategist and a support and training lead. You report to the Engagement Manager on your account, with a dotted line to the regional Senior Director, Growth Strategy for career development. Your day-to-day is set by your customer's needs, not by a central engineering sprint. Travel to customer site is expected — typically 30–50% of your time, sometimes more during go-live. When not on-site, you're in our Gurugram office with the other forward deployed engineers, peer-reviewing each other's configurations and comparing patterns across accounts. The progression path is clear. Senior forward deployed engineers become Engagement Managers. Exceptional ones carve out a platform area of their own and move into our product engineering team. A subset move onto the AI platform team as agent engineers. This is the single largest source of senior technical talent we expect to develop over the next three years. title: Director, Engineering
jobDescription:
A platform is only as strong as its pillars. Someone has to own each one — architecting it, setting the tests and observability bar, picking which battles to fight and which to defer, and leading the engineers who ship within it. That's the Director, Engineering. Your pillar could be the agent orchestration layer, the workflow runtime, the routing and optimisation engine, the TMS/WMS core, the integration fabric, or a new primitive we haven't built yet. You pick up to two in conversation with us, then you own them. This is not a role where you ship tickets from a sprint. It's a role where you make the bets that determine whether Shipsy's platform can handle the next 10x — of customers, shipments, and agents. You lead a small team (3–6 engineers), and the team's work and yours are interwoven — you write code, you review code, and you hold the technical vision for what gets built next. What you'll own A pillar. One major area of the Shipsy platform. You own the technical direction, the architectural decisions, the interfaces it exposes, and the bar it's held to. System design. When a problem crosses multiple pillars, you're the engineer who sketches the design that ships. You reason about failure modes, latency budgets, data contracts, and operational cost before anyone writes a line of code. A small team. You lead 3–6 engineers — hiring them, running their design reviews, coaching them through tough debugging, and raising their bar on every code review. Their growth is your growth. Productising the FDE flywheel. Your pillar is where field-tested patterns become platform. You pair with Forward Deployed Engineers, read their code, and decide what belongs in the platform and what stays bespoke. Technical storytelling. You can explain why an architecture choice matters — to a junior engineer, to the CEO, and to a customer CIO. All three audiences, same clarity. Unblocking. You're the engineer the team pages when something breaks that no one else knows how to fix. You don't solve every bug — you make sure the team can. Scaling the engineering function. We're going from 30 engineers to 100+ over the next two years. Directors define the patterns and playbooks that make that scale work. Who we're looking for 5–8 years of production engineering experience at a high-growth technology company — unicorn, scaled startup, or a top-tier big-tech team. You've seen a codebase grow from 20 engineers to 200 and know why most of the scars came from. Tier-1 education. IIT / NIT / BITS / equivalent, or a top international institution. You've owned a system at scale. Not "worked on a team that owned one" — you've been the person whose name was on the on-call rotation when it broke. Deep generalist. One area you're world-class in (distributed systems, ML infra, databases, agent runtimes, etc.) and the range to credibly step into any adjacent area. No narrow single-domain specialists. You think clearly about where AI helps. First principles about where AI changes the shape of a problem, not where to add a chat interface. You've built with Claude, GPT, and agent frameworks. You understand evals, tool use, and long-running orchestration. Taste in architecture. You can articulate why one design is better than another along cost, correctness, latency, and evolvability. You resist cleverness. Track record of making engineers better. The people you've worked with got materially sharper because of you — not just shipped more. Specific names, specific before-and-after. High agency and low ego. You can push back on a CEO in a design review and take feedback from a junior engineer in a code review. Both, on the same day. Where the role sits You own a pillar on the Core Platform team, based out of Gurugram. Your first pillar is agreed in the offer letter — we're explicit about which bet you're signing up for and how we'll measure it in 12 months. You report to the engineering leadership, with a direct line into the product and Forward Deployed Engineering leads. No manager layers between you and the strategic work. You'll work side-by-side with Engagement Managers and FDEs when a customer need surfaces a gap in the platform — you're the engineer who decides whether to fill it, work around it, or defer it. Progression is deliberate. Director → Senior Director with an expanded pillar and larger team, or Director → founding engineer on a new product bet, or Director → VP Engineering as the function scales. We're building the next ten years of the engineering org from this hire inwards — the technical leaders we need in 2030 are the ones we're picking today. title: Software Engineer, Core Platform
jobDescription:
The best engineers aren't slotted into a pillar on day one. They're given the highest-impact problem on the platform and expected to work it with rigour. Generalist-first, specialist-later. That's the model here. Core engineering sits at the centre of the Shipsy flywheel. Forward Deployed Engineers prove patterns inside a customer. Product leaders frame the long-term bets. Your job is to turn those signals into platform — productising what deserves to be productised, and building new primitives where the platform is thin. The pillars you could work on are: Agent Fleet (the agent orchestration layer), Agent Flow (the workflow runtime), the TMS and WMS cores, the routing and optimisation engine, the integration fabric, and the data platform underneath all of it. Where you start depends on where you fit and where the leverage is — not on a slot we filled six months ago. What you'll own Module-level design. Given a problem, you own the design, the build, the tests, the deploy, the on-call. No hand-off to a platform team on the other side of the building — you are the platform team. Production code at scale. Everything you ship runs against 5 billion+ shipments a year. Performance, correctness, and observability are not afterthoughts — they are the job. Productising the FDE flywheel. A Forward Deployed Engineer proves something inside one customer. You take the pattern, generalise it, and make it a platform primitive that works for the next ten. API and interface design. Integration partners, FDEs, and customers use the surfaces you design. Clean, stable, well-documented APIs are the bar — not the aspiration. Code review and pattern-setting. We're small enough that every engineer reviews every engineer. The standards of the codebase are what you and your peers decide they are. Scaling yourself. Use Claude, GPT, and agent frameworks aggressively in your own workflow. The person on the team who has automated more of their own work than anyone else wins. Picking your pillar. After your first six months, you'll have seen enough of the platform to decide where you want to go deep. Generalist-first, specialist-later. Who we're looking for We're not hiring a specialist in any single stack. We're hiring an engineer with strong foundations who can be thrown at any part of the platform and be productive inside a fortnight. 2–4 years of production engineering. You've shipped code to real users at meaningful scale — not a single internship or a coursework project. Tier-1 education. IIT / NIT / BITS / equivalent, or a top international institution. Strong fundamentals. Data structures, algorithms, systems thinking. You can design a schema, reason about a distributed failure, and instrument a slow endpoint without a runbook. Generalist instincts. You've worked across backend, frontend, infra, or data and can move between them. No "I only do backend." High agency. You've picked a project, owned it end-to-end, and shipped it without a PM spec pushing you. Ideally you've also built something outside work — a side project, open source, or a company. You use AI tools in your work. Hands-on with Claude, GPT, and agent frameworks. We'll ask what you've actually built, not what you've read about. Taste. You can tell the difference between a 100-line function that's clean and a 100-line function that's a maintenance nightmare — and you can explain why. Where the role sits You're on the Core Platform team, based out of Gurugram. Your first rotation is assigned based on where you fit and where the highest-leverage problem is right now. After six months you can request a pillar move, or you can stay and go deep — your call. You pair frequently with Forward Deployed Engineers. They see the customer pain first, you productise the fix. It's a closed feedback loop, on purpose — the engineers who do this well become the ones who shape the next version of the platform. You report to a Staff Engineer and have a skip-level with engineering leadership. No manager overhead. title: Head of Global Partnerships & Alliances
jobDescription:
Shipsy runs the logistics operations of some of the world's largest enterprises. Most rollouts are 12 to 24 month transformations involving services, integration, and change management. Today our Growth Strategy team delivers that work directly. To scale, we need partners. Strategy firms to diagnose. Global SIs to deploy. Technology partners to extend the platform. Referral partners to open new doors. The Head of Global Partnerships & Alliances builds and leads that ecosystem. You define the partner strategy across all four tracks, sign and activate the right firms, and make sure every joint customer wins. Enterprise buyers spend roughly four dollars on services for every dollar on software. The partner motion is how Shipsy captures that downstream value while accelerating the customer's outcome. This is a from-scratch global build. The Shipsy partner programme is live, the four tracks are defined, and the first signatures are in. The next phase is yours to scope, staff, and own. If you have led complex global engagements at a top-tier consulting firm and want to move into building rather than advising, this is the role. What you'll own The partner strategy. Which firms we work with, in which regions, on which use cases. You set the framework, the targets, and the operating cadence. Tier-1 alliance relationships. You personally own the relationships with our most strategic global SIs and strategy firms. CXO at Accenture, Partner at Mc Kinsey, Senior Partner at Pw C. These are your accounts. A team you build over time. You start as the player-coach, then hire regional partner managers and partner marketing as the motion proves out. Year one is signing and activating. You have worked alongside system integrators, technology vendors, or subcontractors to deliver joint engagements.
